Md. Nurul Haq with AKM Shahidul Huq, Advocates ------ For the Petitioner.
Ziaur Rahman Khan, Advocate ------ For the Respondent Nos. 1-2.
HR Sharif ------ For the Respondent Nos. 6-14
parties:
Anwar Ali (Md) ------ Petitioner 
Vs. 
Chairman, Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakha (RAJUK) & others ------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
Mainur Reza Chowdhury, J. : This Rule Nisi was issued on the respondents to show cause why the notice dated 26.12.88 (Annexure-F) issued by the Authorised Officer, Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakha respondent No. 2 should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect.

2. The case of the petitioner is that the petitioner, Proprietor of New Lucky Hardware Store has been carrying on business at Municipal Holding No. 2, English Road, Roy Shah Bazar Dhaka (hereinafter called the premises). The respondent Nos. 6-14 are the present owners of the premises. The premises were constructed with pucca floor, walls with tin roof and were let out to the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioner by the predecessor-in-interest of the respondent Nos. 6-14 before the promulgation of the Building Construction Act, 1952. The petitioner paid rent regularly for the premises to the owners. The lands of the premises along with the other lands were acquired by the Government of erstwhile East Pakistan for the purpose of development of Dolaikhal area and the people of the locality and the petitioner filed writ petitions against the Dhaka Improvement Trust. A compromise was arrived at by which the Dhaka Improvement Trust agreed to accommodate the occupiers running small industries and business at suitable places, so the petitions were not pressed and rules were discharged. The present petitioner's petition was Writ Petition No. 361/66 which was disposed of on 3.3.67. The Dhaka Improvement Trust (now Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakha) acquired only so much land as would be necessary for construction of 100 ft. wide road. The land of the petitioner's landlord and land of the predecessor-in-interest of the present owners respondent Nos. 6-14 were not acquired, so the petitioner and others continued to do their business. In 1971 all constructions on both the sides of Dolaikhal were burnt to ashes by the then Pakistan Army and after liberation the petitioner and other tenants re-constructed their shop premises in the same places where they were originally running their business. In the meantime the Government developed the area by constructing a wide road foot-path and road-side garden as a result of which the value of the area increased and so the owners of the premises respondent Nos. 6-14 began to conspire to evict the petitioner from the premises. The owners having refused to accept the rent from the petitioner, he deposited the same with the Rent Controller in Rent Control Case No. 1/87. Thereafter the owners respondent Nos. 6-14 were planning to forcibly evict the petitioner from the premises as a result of which the petitioner filed Title Suit No. 104/87 in the 6th Court of Assistant Judge, Dhaka for permanent injunction restraining the owners from forcibly evicting the petitioner from the premises and the Court was pleased to issue show cause notice. The owners then planned and succeeded in improperly inducing the officers of Rajdhani Unnayan Kartipakha (RAJUK) particularly its Authorised Officer (Respondent No. 2) to issue a notice of eviction upon the petitioner and other tenants. The owners in collusion with Respondent No. 2, the Authorised Officer of RAJUK are said to have suppressed the first notice. There after Respondent No. 6 Md. Matiur Rahman, one of the owners on 13.8.87 issued a notice upon the petitioner to vacate the premises within 7 days as the same was "unauthorised construction" referring therein to a show cause notice of RAJUK under section 3B of the Building Construction Act, 1952.

3. Thereafter the Authorised Officer of RAJUK respondent No. 2 issued the impugned notice dated 26.12.88 (Annexure-F) on the petitioner under section 3B of the Building Construction Act 1952 to vacate the premises within 7 days as the premises would be dismantled. The said notice (Annexure-F) reads as follows:

“যেহেতু সুত্রেল্লিকিত স্মারক মোতাবেক আপনাকে/আপনাদিগকে কারণ দর্শানোর জন্য নির্দেশ দেওয়া হইয়াছিল এবং সেহেতু আপনি/আপনারা নির্ধারিত সময়ের মধ্যে কারণ দর্শাইতে ব্যর্থ হইয়াছেন। যেহেতু বি,সি, কমিটি এই মর্মে সন্তষ্ট হইয়াচেন যে, আপনি/আপনার ইমারত নির্মাণ (সংশোধন) আইন ১৯৮৭ এর ৩ ধারা লংঘন করিয়া সি,এস,দাগ নং-মৌজা শহর এলাকা হোল্ডিং নং-২ ইংলিশ রোড নির্মিত ইমারতের একজন দখলদার।

সেহেতু বি,সি, কমিটির সিদ্ধান্ত মোতাবেক আপনাকে/আপনাদিগকে এই আদেশ প্রত্র প্রাপ্তির ৭ দিনের মধ্যে অনুমোদিত ইমারত খালি করিয়া দিবার নির্দেশ দেওয়া যাইতেছে। অন্যথায় আমারত নির্মাণ (সংশোধন) আইন ১৯৮৭ এর ৭ ধারা মোতাবেক উক্ত অনুমোদিত ইমারতাদি ভাংগিয়া ফেলিয়া আপনার/আপনাদের নিকট হইতে ভাংগিবার খরচ আদায় করা হইবে।

অথরাইজড অফিসার

রাজধানী উন্নয়ন কর্তৃপক্ষ, ঢাকা।

4. On receipt of the said notice the petitioner made an appeal on 28.12.88(Annexure-G) to respondent No. 2 the Authorised Officer stating, inter-alia. that he had not received his earlier show cause notice dated 23.12.88 and the petitioner and others were occupying the premises and were running business therein for about 30 years, that after the shops on the premises were burnt down by the Pakistan Army after military crackdown on 25.3.71, the petitioner and other tenants had to construct the shops at their own cost with the permission of the owners (Respondent No. 6, etc.), that when Respondent No. 6 and other owners refused to accept rent and issue receipts, the petitioners started depositing rent in the Court of the Rent Controller, but their representation appeal was not considered. On 25.2.89 the officer of the RAJUK threatened the petitioner by making announcement on microphone that the petitioner and other tenants would be forcibly evicted from the alleged unauthorised constructions.

5. Being aggrieved by the said notice dated 26.12.88 (Annexure-F) for eviction the petitioner rued this petition and obtained the present Rule Nisi.

6. The respondent by filing affidavit-in-opposition have controverted the contention raised by the petitioner. The Chairman and the Authorised Officer of RAJUK respondent Nos. 1 and 2 stated, inter alia, that the premises were constructed without any sanctioned plan and the petitioner and others having admitted to have re-constructed the shops after liberation without permission of the Dhaka Improvement Trust after they were burnt down by the Pak Army after military crackdown on 25.3.1971, the unauthorised constructions come squarely within the mischief of section 3B of the Building Construction Act, 1952 and the construction being unauthorised were liable to be dismantled. They have further stated that the fact that the petitioner was carrying on lawful business in the premises is no concern to the RAJUK. They were only to see whether the building and structures were constructed with sanction or not and to direct their removal if they were unauthorised.

7. The owners of the premises respondent Nos. 6-14 have, inter alia, stated that it was they who reconstructed the premises after liberation after it was destroyed by the Pakistan Army after the military crackdown on 25.3.1971 and not the petitioners and, as the reconstruction was urgently required the approval of the Authorised Officer under the Building Construction Act, 1952 could not be taken. The owners have not denied the show cause notice issued to them by the respondent No. 2 under section 3B of the Building Construction Act. 1952.

8. Mr. Md. Nurul Huq, the learned Advocate for the petitioner, submitted that RAJUK represented by respondent Nos. 1 and 2 could not direct a tenant to vacate a tenanted premises even if the premises was found to have been constructed without any sanctioned plan as required by Building Construction Act 1952. He argued that a premises which was not constructed with sanctioned plan was a matter between the landlord (owner of the premises) and RAJUK. The tenant-petitioner could only be evicted by the landlord that is the respondent Nos. 6-14 under the provisions of the Premises Rent Control Act with notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act. He also submitted that if there had been a violation of section 3 of the Building Construction Act. 1952 then RAJUK could take penal action against the owners of the premises under section 12 of the Act but could not direct the petitioner tenant to vacate the premises for such violation. He has further submitted that the notice was malafide as the petitioner had been discriminated against as others in the neighbourhood had not been served with any such notice.

9. Mr. Ziaur Rahman Khan, the learned Advocate for respondent Nos. 1 and 3, submitted that in view of the clear provision of section 3 of the Building Construction Act. 1952 that no one was permitted to make any construction of any structure within the Greater Dhaka City area without obtaining a sanctioned plan from the Authorised Officer of the RAJUK, and, as admittedly the premises in the present case was constructed without sanction, the respondents had the authority to direct the owner, the occupier and the person in charge of the building to show cause under section 3B of the Building Construction Act 1952 within at least seven days why the premises should not be removed or dismantled. Further, as required under section 6 of the said Act, the respondent No. 2 simultaneously with the notice under section 3B could issue a notice on the occupier to vacate the building or premises within the period mentioned therein. Therefore, the impugned order Annexure-F dated 26.12.88 issued by the respondent No. 2 on the petitioner, who was the occupier of the premises to vacate the premises, for the purpose of demolition was lawful.

10. Before considering the submissions made by the learned Advocates it is necessary to consider as a whole the provisions of sections 3, 3B, 6 and 7 of the Building Construction Act. 1952 which are as follows:

"3. Restriction on construction of building and excavation of tank.

(1) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, or in any agreement, no person shall, without the previous sanction of an Authorised Officer, construct or reconstruct or make addition or alteration to any building or excavate re-excavate any tank or cut or raze any hill within the area to which this Act applies; and such sanction shall be subject to such terms and conditions as the Authorised Officer may deem fit to impose:

Provided that such sanction shall remain valid for three years from the date of sanction and on the expiry of the period the applicant shall have to apply for and obtain a fresh sanction.

(la) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) all sanctions obtained during the 12 months immediately preceding the 30th September. 1958 shall be deemed to have expired and no such construction or excavation shall be made without obtaining fresh sanction.

Explanation:-For the purpose of obtaining fresh sanction under sub-section (1) or sub-section (Ia), no fresh sanction shall have to be obtained for the construction of building where the construction has been made up to 4 feet above plinth level.

(2) The Government may by notification in the Official Gazette. direct that the power of an Authorised Officer under sub-section (1) shall be exercised by a Committee in such area as may be specified in the notification.

(3) When a notification under sub-section (2) has been issued the Authorised Officer shall not exercise the power conferred on him by sub-section (1) in the area to which they said notification relates.

(4) The provisions of sub-section (1) shall not apply to normal repairs to existing building.

3B. Direction for removal of construction etc:

(1) Where it appears to the Authorised Officer or the Committee as the case may be that:

(a) any building has been constructed or re-constructed or any addition or alteration to any building has been made or any tank has been excavated or re-excavated, before or after the commencement of the Building Construction (Amendment) Ordinance 1986 (Ordinance No. LXXII of 1986).

(b) any building is being constructed or reconstructed or any addition or alteration to any building is being made or any tank is being excavated or re-excavated without obtaining the sanction under section 3 or in breach of any of the terms or conditions subject to which sanction was granted under that section he or it may by a notice direct the owner the occupier and the person in charge of the building or the tank to show cause within such period not being less than seven days as may be mentioned in the notice why:

(i) the building or any portion thereof whether constructed or under construction as may be specified in the notice should not be removed or dismantled; or

(ii) the tank or any portion thereof whether excavated or under excavation specified in the notice should not be filled up; or

(iii) further construction or re-construction of or addition or alteration to the building or excavation or re-excavation of the tank should not be stopped.

(2) Where a person is asked by a notice under sub-section (1) to show cause why further construction or re-construction of or addition or alteration to any building or excavation or re-excavation of any tank should not be stopped he shall stop such further construction or re-construction or addition or alteration or excavation or re-excavation, as the case may be, from the date the notice is served on him till an order is made under sub-section (3).

(3) Where after considering the cause shown if any within the time mentioned in the notice and giving the person showing the cause a reasonable opportunity of being heard or where no cause is shown within such time the Authorised Officer or the Committee as the case may be after such inquiry as he or it deems fit is satisfied that the building has been or is being constructed or re-constructed. or addition or alteration to the building has been or is being made or the tank has been or is being excavated or re-excavated without obtaining the sanction under section 3 or in breach of any of the terms and conditions subject to which sanction was granted under that section he or it may by an order in writing stating reasons thereof direct the owner. the occupier and the person in charge of the building or the tank to remove or dismantle the building or any portion thereof or to fill up the tank or any portion thereof as specified in the order within such time as may be fixed by him or it or to stop further construction or re- construction addition or alteration or excavation or re-excavation, as the case may be; and otherwise shall make an order vacating the notice.

(4) Where further construction or re-construction of or addition or alteration to. any building or excavation or re-excavation of any tank has been stopped under sub-section (2) and cause is shown within the time mentioned in the notice against the stoppage of such further construction or re-construction addition or alteration excavation or re-excavation, as the case may be the Authorised Officer or the Committee as the case may be shall make his or its order under sub-section (3) within fifteen days from the date the cause is shown.

(5) No order under this section shall be made directing any person to remove or dismantle any building or part thereof or fill up any tank or part thereof unless it is found that:

(a) such building or part thereof has been constructed or re-constructed or such tank or part thereof has been excavated or re-excavated at a place or in a manner which is contrary to the master plan or development plan if any of the area in which the building or the tank is situated or

(b) such building or part thereof cannot be reconstructed or altered or such tank or part thereof cannot be re-excavated, in accordance with the terms and conditions of the sanction alleged to have been breached or

(c) such building or part thereof or such tank or part thereof causes any undue inconvenience in respect of use or occupation of any land or building or road or passage in the area adjacent to it, or

(d) sanction if prayed for could not be granted for the construction or re-construction of or addition or alteration to the building or excavation or re-excavation of the tank provided such person :

(i) pays within the time specified by the Authorised Officer or the Committee as the case may be a fine of an amount, which shall not be less than Tk. 5000 and more than Tk. 50.000 to be determined by that Officer or the Committee.

(ii) makes necessary addition or alteration to the building or makes the excavation or the filling up of the tank as may be directed by the Authorised Officer or the Committee within the time specified by that Officer or the Committee and

(iii) obtains the necessary sanction on payment of a fee which shall be ten times the amount of the prescribed.

(6) If a person fails to pay the fine or make the addition or alteration or excavation or filling or obtain the sanction as mentioned in sub-section (5) within the time specified by the Authorised Officer or the Committee as the case may be under that sub-section they said officer or the Committee may, by an order in writing direct the owner the occupier and the person in charge of the building or the tank to remove or dismantle the building or any portion thereof or fill up the tank or any portion thereof as specified in the order within such time as may be fixed by him or it.

(7) A notice or an order under this section shall be served in the prescribed manner.

6. Eviction of occupier:-(I) The Authorised Officer or the Committee as the case may be shall simultaneously with the issue of an order under section 3B or a notice under section 4 or sub-section (1) of section 5 on the owner the occupier or the person in charge of the building as the case may be, issue a notice upon them to vacate the building within the period mentioned therein or within such further period as may be extended by the Authorised Officer or the Committee.

(2) If the person upon whom a notice to vacate the building under sub-section (1) has been served does not in pursuance of the notice vacate the building within the period mentioned in the notice he shall notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force be liable to be summarily evicted there from by the Authorised Officer or the Committee, as the case may be and the Authorised Officer or the Committee may, in effecting such eviction, use or cause to be used such force as may be deemed necessary.

7. Removal of building, etc:-(I) If any person fails to comply with any direction for removal or dismantling of any building or any portion thereof, or filling up any tank or any portion thereof, given to him under section 3B, within the period fixed thereof, the Authorised Officer of the Committee, as the case may be, may cause the building or portion thereof to be removed or the tank or portion thereof to be filled up, as the case may be, by using or causing to be used such force as may be deemed necessary; and the cost thus incurred shall be realised from its owner in the manner laid down for recovery of fine under section 386 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 (Act V of 1898).

(2) If any person fails to comply with any direction for removal of any building given to him under section 4 or sub-section (1) of section 5, within the period fixed therefor, the Authorised Officer may cause the temporary building or the building under construction, as the case may be, to be removed at his own expenses in which case such person shall not be any more entitled to any compensation. "

11. From the provisions of section 3 we find that no person without the previous sanction of respondent No.2, the Authorised Officer, RAJUK can construct any building in the greater Dhaka City. The petitioner has claimed that his predecessors had been carrying on business before the Building Construction Act, 1952 came into effect and so there could not have been any violation of section 3 of the Act. However, we find from paragraph 6 of Annexure-G dated 28.12.88 of the application as well as from the affidavit-in-reply submitted by the petitioner that the premises having been burnt down in 1971 by the Pakistani Army the shop building was reconstructed in the premises after liberation and neither the petitioner-tenant nor the owners claim to have obtained sanction of the plan. The respondent Nos. 6-14, the owners, in their affidavit-in-opposition have denied that the petitioner reconstructed the premises. The respondents claimed that they constructed the premises after liberation after it was destroyed by the Pakistani Army in 1971, but admit that when the premises were reconstructed they could not take sanction of the plan from the respondents No. 1 and 2. It is, therefore, clear that the existing premises were constructed after liberation, that is, after the Building Construction Act, 1952came into effect, without obtaining an) sanction from the respondent Nos. 1 and 2. Therefore, the construction of the premises without obtaining sanction was a violation of section 3 of the Act.

12. Section 3B which was inserted by Building Construction (Amendment) Act, 1987 (Act No. XII of 1987), inter alia, provides that when a building has been constructed without obtaining the sanction under section 3, the Authorised Officer may by a notice direct the owner, the occupier and man-in-charge of the building to show cause within such period, not being less than seven days, as may be mentioned in the notice why the building should not be removed or dismantled. The respondent Nos. 1 and 2 claimed that the notices under section 3B of the Building Construction Act, 1952 for removal of unauthorised construction were legally and validly issued and served upon the owners and occupiers first on 23.11.88 and then again on 26.12.88. The petitioner admits to have received the impugned notice dated 26.12.88 (Annexure-F) and the petitioner and other tenants also made representation (Annexure-G dated 28.12.88) to respondent No. 2, the Authorised Officer. It also appears from his petitions that the owners through Respondent No. 6 Matiur Rahman (one of the owners) as early as on 13.8.87 through letter Annexure E dated 13.8.87 had informed the petitioner Ansar Ali that RAJUK had served a notice on him under section 3B of the Building Construction (Amendment) Act, 1987 and that the petitioner tenant should comply with the instruction of RAJUK within 7 days. Further, challenging the notice dated 26.12.88 (Annexure-F) the petitioner obtained this Rule Nisi on 10.4.89. Therefore the petitioner undoubtedly had sufficient notice and opportunity of being heard. The petitioner all along knew that no sanction had been obtained for the construction of the premises and therefore knew or ought to have known that it was liable to be dismantled for violation of section 3 of the Act. In any case since the petitioner admittedly is only a tenant it is not necessary for him to reply to the show cause notice in respect of the premises constructed without obtaining sanction or agree to pay fine for unauthorised construction or show cause why it should not be dismantled or removed; but the petitioner and other tenants did give reply Annexure-'C' dated 28.12.88 claiming to have reconstructed the shop building after liberation, but never claimed to have obtained permission of Respondent No. 2 the Authorised Officer. These questions and other questions involved in the said section 3B are essentially for the owners or owners to reply, and in this case the owners respondent Nos. 6-14 do not deny that they received such notice from RAJUK through respondent No. 2 Mr. Ziaur Rahman Khan, the learned Advocate had submitted that as RAJUK does not always know who the owner of a building is, section 3B also provides for serving show cause notice on the occupier and the person in charge of the building so that the notice reaches or comes to knowledge of the owner of the building. Further, it gives the occupier notice that he would have to vacate the premises which is constructed without sanction and which unauthorised construction would be required to be removed or dismantled. He (occupier) is then served with the notice to vacate under section 6 of the Act which (Annexure-F dated 26.12.88) the petitioner in this case had undoubtedly received.

<u>13. The provisions in sections 3B and 6 clearly give power to the Authorised Officer of the RAJUK to serve notice on the occupier and to direct him to vacate any building constructed without sanction by the owner. Therefore, the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the petitioner that since the petitioner was a tenant of the owners, only the owners could evict him under the Premises Rent Control Act after giving notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act is not tenable. This may have been true if the building was constructed without violating the provisions of the Building Construction Act, 1952 as amended in 1987. In this case, admittedly the premises was constructed without obtaining sanction from RAJUK and therefore Respondent No. 2 validly passed the impugned order Annexure F dated 26.12.88 under the Building Construction Act, 1952 for occupying such a building.</u>

14. We find from the provisions of section 6 of the Building Construction Act that the respondent No.2 may direct an occupier to vacate a premises simultaneously with a notice under section 3B. In the present case respondent No. 2 having received no reply to his notice dated 23.11.90 either from the owner or from the occupier, the occupier is liable to be directed to vacate the premises which has been constructed without obtaining .sanction for dismantling.

In the circumstances stated above we do not find that the impugned order dated 26.12.88 (Annexure-F) issued by the respondent No. 2, the Authorised Officer, RAJUK on the petitioner to vacate the premises, is in any way illegal or without lawful authority.

In the result, the Rule is discharged but without any order as to costs. The stay order passed by this court is vacated.

End.
